issues.issue: The carve-out preserving "any limitations defenses which may exist immediately before this agreement is executed" does not say whether it merely preserves accrued elapsed time or lets Lincoln General argue the Excess Funds Claims were already time-barred. That distinction is the classic tolling-agreement construction fight.

The reservation of pre-existing limitations defenses pulls against the preceding sentence's unqualified agreement to toll the statute of limitations for the Excess Funds Claims until the Lawsuit is finally resolved. Whether the toll or the reservation controls a partly-run period must be harmonised.

"During the pendency of the Lawsuit" is undefined and may end at judgment or only after appeals, which controls when U.S. Auto may file its separate suit. The neighbouring tolling sentence uses a different, longer formulation.

The filing bar's "pendency" trigger does not match the tolling clause's "settled or otherwise finally resolved, including the completion of any appeals," leaving a possible gap between when tolling stops and when filing becomes permissible. The two sentences must be read together.

The Defendants' stipulation that the Other Causes of Action share no nucleus of operative facts with the Lawsuit is in tension with the scope paragraph, which retains overlapping claims about the same reinsured policies and IBNR. A preclusion or claim-splitting argument would require reconciling them.

This express waiver of preclusion defences sits against the closing paragraph, in which all parties "reserve the right to contest any later-filed separate lawsuits" and may assert "any and all applicable defenses or affirmative defenses." A court would have to decide which sentence prevails as to res judicata.

The Defendants' toll runs until final resolution including appeals, while the earlier sentence bars Lincoln General from filing only "during the pendency of the Lawsuit," so the protected window and the filing bar may not coincide. The two must be read together to know when suit is safe.

The preservation of "any limitations defenses which may exist immediately before this agreement is executed" leaves unclear whether the Defendants may still contend the Other Causes of Action were already barred notwithstanding the toll. That is the standard latent ambiguity in a tolling carve-out.

The carve-out pulls against the immediately preceding unqualified promise to toll limitations for the Other Causes of Action until final resolution. Which controls a period that had partly run at execution is a genuine reconciliation question.

The qualifier "in general" is inserted into an otherwise absolute non-concession, leaving open whether some specific concession of party status was intended elsewhere in the letter. A reader cannot tell what the words carve out.

The blanket reservation of "any and all applicable defenses or affirmative defenses" is a general catch-all with no carve-out for the defences the letter expressly waives, so its reach against the earlier waivers is uncertain. The sentence also omits the noun qualifying "allegations" after "defenses to."

This reservation directly contradicts the express waivers of res judicata and collateral estoppel by Lincoln General and by Defendants, and the mutual tolling promises, since limitations and preclusion are "applicable defenses." A court would have to decide whether the general reservation swallows the specific waivers.
